newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, mkt awaits Dadas hearing.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, mkt awaits Dadas hearing.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.9 percent on Wednesday following a report that the stock exchange had decided to bar the public from a hearing involving brokerage Dadas.

Some traders said they expected the stock exchange's honorary court would eventually decide to ban Dadas from trading. The court has indicted Dadas for allegedly rigging prices by trading among its affiliated companies.
"News that the honorary court of the Ljubljana bourse will keep its procedure against brokerage Dadas closed to the public brought uncertainty to the market," a trader said.
But he did not rule out a rally in early September when investors are expected to return to the market in numbers.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 8.99 points to 984,65.
* Six shares fell and nine rose, while eight were untraded.
* Turnover eased to 50.4 million tolars from 74.6 million.
* Pharmaceutical company Salus had the highest turnover and was the biggest gainer, rising 21.35 percent to 12,703 tolars on volume of 1,150 shares for total turnover of 14.6 million tolars.
* Bank Probanka was the leading decliner, falling 4.20 percent to 14,935 on volume of 575 shares for total turnover of 8.6 million tolars.
* Financial consultancy Dadas, which owns brokerage Dadas, fell 3.2 percent to 32,790 on volume of 149 shares on voolume of 4.9 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
